purpose: Make the v3 specification's own exclusion categories operative on a snapshot that is more than a year newer than the closed ticker lists the v1 rules are built from, without touching the immutable v1 or v2 artifacts and without letting any asset enter or leave the batch by hand.

problem.statement: The v1 exclusion_rules block is a closed list of tickers. It can only name instruments that existed when it was frozen, so the six categories the v3 specification names in universe.exclusions are not actually applied to instruments issued since then.
problem.consequence_if_unaddressed: Applied unchanged, the rules admit fiat-pegged stablecoins, cash-management and treasury funds and tokenized gold into the v3 batch. Such instruments have no breakout structure, so the batch would be diluted with assets that cannot produce the event the study measures.

observed_in_the_frozen_v3_snapshot.note: The count is a property of the frozen snapshot and of the published markers. It is recorded, not tuned: no marker was added or removed after seeing a validation outcome or a strategy result, because no candle had been fetched and no result existed when this amendment was authored.

decision.rule: The v1 exclusion_rules block is applied verbatim, and the v3 classifier below is applied in addition to it. An asset is excluded when either the inherited fixed list or the classifier matches it.
decision.why_an_amendment_and_not_an_edit: configs/research_v3.json is frozen and hash-bound, and the snapshot it governs has already been retrieved. Changing the specification after the retrieval would silently re-time the rule set. A versioned amendment keeps the specification and the snapshot exactly as they were and records the correction separately, with its own hash.
decision.why_a_published_classifier_and_not_a_lis: A second hand-written ticker list would move the same problem to the next snapshot. A published marker rule is applied mechanically to every snapshot entry, is re-derivable by anyone who has the amendment, and produces the same answer for every asset rather than for the assets somebody thought of.
what_is_deliberately_not_changed: the inherited fixed lists are applied unchanged
the exchange_tokens and low_liquidity_or_new groups are not extended: the v3 specification's universe.exclusions does not name them, so this amendment does not invent an exclusion category
the market-capitalization floor, the prior-universe identity rule and the ordering rule are not touched
no v1 or v2 artifact is modified

match_semantics.text_marker: case-insensitive substring of the lower-cased concatenation of the snapshot entry's 'name' and 'id' fields
match_semantics.symbol_exact: case-insensitive exact equality with the upper-cased snapshot entry's 'symbol' field
match_semantics.group_precedence: the inherited fixed lists are evaluated first, then the classifier groups in the published group_order; the first group that matches an entry is the recorded exclusion group
match_semantics.application_scope: the classifier is applied to every entry of the frozen snapshot, not only to the entries that reach the batch, so the derived exclusion set is complete and the same rule applies to every asset

stablecoins.rationale: Fiat-pegged stablecoins, cash-management and money-market funds, short-duration treasury funds, tokenized gold and every other instrument that a marker names. A stablecoin has no breakout structure, so admitting one would dilute the batch with assets that cannot produce the event the study measures.

wrapped_bridged.rationale: Wrapped, bridged and staked representations of another asset are not independent assets: their price tracks the underlying and their history duplicates it.

leveraged_synthetic.rationale: Leveraged and hedged tokens carry a path-dependent payoff and a decaying premium, so their candles are not a breakout asset.

synthetic_tokens.rationale: Tokenized claims on a real-world equity are synthetic instruments: they track an equity market, not a crypto market, and their candles contain no crypto breakout.

derivative_tokens.rationale: A token that is a derivative of another instrument inherits that instrument's price path and is not an independent asset.

inherited_fixed_lists.note: Applied verbatim, as the v3 specification's eligibility_validation.exclusion_rules requires. The v3 classifier is additional to these lists and never overrides them.

application_order: 1. the inherited fixed lists (v1 exclusion_rules), symbol by symbol
2. the v3 classifier groups, in the published group_order
3. the prior-universe identity rules (Binance symbol, CoinGecko id, rename marker in the name)
5. descending market capitalization, truncated to top_n

floor.recompute_rule: the floor is the minimum market_cap_usd over the eligible_assets of research/universe_manifest_v2.json; it is recomputed from that manifest and never trusted from the specification

prior_universe.rule: An asset is already in a prior universe when its Binance symbol, its CoinGecko id or the old ticker of a rename marker in its name occurs in the eligible assets of the v1 or the v2 universe manifest.

identity_rules.statement: the upper-cased ticker of the snapshot entry occurs in a prior universe
the CoinGecko id of the snapshot entry occurs in a prior universe

the name carries a rename marker of the form '(ex-<TICKER>)' and <TICKER> occurs in a prior universe. A rename can come with a new provider id, so the id rule alone does not catch it: MATIC (CoinGecko id 'matic-network') is POL (CoinGecko id 'polygon-ecosystem-token') in the frozen v3 snapshot.

corrections_to_the_specification.specification_text: A renamed asset keeps its CoinGecko id and is therefore the same asset.
corrections_to_the_specification.problem: The sentence is not true in general: a provider that renames an asset may also issue a new id. In the frozen v3 snapshot MATIC (id 'matic-network', a v1 candidate) is POL (id 'polygon-ecosystem-token').
corrections_to_the_specification.correction: The published identity_rules above are the operative rule. The rename marker rule identifies the renamed successor, so POL is excluded as already_in_prior_universe and the v3 batch contains no asset of the v1 or the v2 universe.
corrections_to_the_specification.why_not_an_edit: configs/research_v3.json is frozen and hash-bound and its snapshot has already been retrieved. The correction is carried here so that the specification and the retrieved snapshot stay exactly as they were.
corrections_to_the_specification.effect_on_the_batch: none: POL's market capitalization is below the batch cutoff, so the derived candidate batch is identical with and without the rename marker rule

derived_classification.note: One record per snapshot entry, in snapshot order, so the derived exclusion set is complete over the whole snapshot and no entry is silently dropped.

derived_candidate_batch.rule: The batch is the top_n eligible assets in strictly descending market-capitalization order, where eligible means: below the recomputed v2 floor, not an asset of the v1 or v2 universe and not excluded by any published rule.

next_version_floor_candidate.note: Informational: the floor of a future universe version is the market capitalization of the lowest-ranked candidate of this version. It is recorded by the expansion log, not applied here.

provenance.statement: The amendment was authored after the market-cap snapshot was retrieved and stored, and before a single v3 candle was fetched, before any candidate was validated against Binance and before any strategy result existed. The markers were chosen from the asset list of the frozen snapshot, which is a fact about the rule, not about a result: the classifier is applied mechanically to all 250 entries, it is published in full, and the derived classification of every entry is recorded here.
provenance.verifier_cross_check: scripts/verify_research_v3_manifests.py recomputes the derived classification from the published markers and the frozen snapshot, and checks that the earliest v3 candle retrieval is later than amendment_timestamp_utc.

not_authorized_by_this_amendment: running a v3 grid, campaign or candidate selection
reading any candle inside the v2 or the v3 confirmatory window
modifying configs/research_v3.json or any v1 or v2 artifact
adding, removing or substituting an asset of the derived candidate batch by hand

hashing.note: amendment_hash is the sha256 of the document body with the amendment_hash key removed. It binds the classifier, the derived classification and the derived candidate batch.
